steps.message:
`routes/users.js:6` is the only place `userId` appears — a one-line change. But it's a breaking change to a published response contract, so I've stopped before editing.

What breaks: `GET /users` returns `userId` to three named consumers — the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export (`README.md:3-5`). Any of them reading `userId` gets `undefined` after the rename. The README also states the project's own rule: "Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint." The consistency argument is real — `/orders` already returns `user_id` — but consistency is what the versioned endpoint is for.

The iOS clients are the sharp edge: shipped app versions can't be redeployed in step with the server.

questions.question: Renaming userId to user_id breaks GET /users for the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the partner export. How should I proceed?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId in the same response. New consumers get the consistent name immediately, existing ones keep working. userId gets removed once the three consumers have migrated. Non-breaking, and the smallest change that gets you the consistency.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README rule literally: add /v2/users returning user_id, leave /users untouched. Cleanest contract story, most work - a new route plus whatever version routing the app doesn't have yet.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Do exactly what you asked: change userId to user_id, nothing else. Breaks the three consumers until each is updated. Choose this if you already know those consumers are handled or the contract note is stale.
